title: The effect of solution-focused counseling on violence rate and quality of life of pregnant women at risk of domestic violence: a randomized controlled trial.

relevance.population: Pregnant women with minor or moderate physical, psychological or sexual domestic violence, living with their spouse.
relevance.exposureEvidence: Pregnant women with minor or moderate physical, psychological or sexual domestic violence, living with their spouse.
relevance.rationale: Psychological intervention with explicitly reported domestic/IPV exposure; mixed-cohort transfer is qualified where applicable.
relevance.transferLimit: See population and limitations; not a population-wide recommendation.

age.reportedRange: Eligibility over 18; mean ages 27.55 and 27.26 years.

setting: A government childbirth-preparation center in Zanjan.

sampleSize.description: See randomized and attrition fields; analyzed is model population when specified.

intervention.provider: Researcher; further credential detail not extracted.

comparator: No additional counselling; delayed sessions offered after follow-up.

outcomes.name: Psychological, minor physical and sexual violence
outcomes.followUp: Six weeks after the six-session course
outcomes.result: Adjusted comparisons favored intervention; severe physical violence did not differ.
outcomes.effectEstimate: Reported p=.001 for each significant violence subscale; effect size and interval not supplied.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

outcomes.name: Quality of life
outcomes.result: Adjusted overall and selected subscales favored intervention; general health and physical/emotional role limitations did not.
outcomes.effectEstimate: Overall p=.001; effect interval not established.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

finding: Several violence subscales and adjusted overall quality of life favored counselling; severe physical violence and several quality-of-life subscales showed no benefit.
limitation: Small single-center, complete-case trial with unmasked self-report and short follow-up; baseline quality of life differed numerically.

design.randomizationEvidence: Random-number table selected permuted blocks of four; 45 participants assigned to each arm.

masking.assessors: Follow-up interviewer explicitly unaware of allocation.

design.crossRationale: One cross: explicit random allocation; double-blinded treatment not established.

quality.riskOfBias: Provisional assessment; allocation, masking and missingness limitations explicitly retained.
quality.attrition: Four nonattenders excluded from intervention and four withdrawals from control; 41 per arm analyzed.
quality.confounding: Random assignment supports group comparison; implementation, missingness and analysis remain relevant.
quality.adverseFindings: Systematic adverse-event assessment not established. Ineligible/excluded women were referred to psychologists.
quality.transferLimits: Small single-center, complete-case trial with unmasked self-report and short follow-up; baseline quality of life differed numerically.

title: Interpersonal psychotherapy delivered by nonspecialists for depression and posttraumatic stress disorder among Kenyan HIV-positive women affected by gender-based violence: Randomized controlled trial.
interventionFamily: Interpersonal psychotherapy integrated with HIV care.

relevance.population: HIV-positive women with gender-based violence exposure, major depression and PTSD; IPV was assessed in the partnered subgroup.
relevance.exposureEvidence: HIV-positive women with gender-based violence exposure, major depression and PTSD; IPV was assessed in the partnered subgroup.
relevance.rationale: Psychological intervention with explicitly reported domestic/IPV exposure; mixed-cohort transfer is qualified where applicable.
relevance.transferLimit: See population and limitations; not a population-wide recommendation.

age.reportedRange: Eligibility at least 18; mean age about 37 years.

sampleSize.description: 256 randomized and included in longitudinal models; partnered baseline subgroup105 (56 IPT,49 control), with changing denominators later.

intervention.description: Interpersonal psychotherapy integrated with HIV care.
intervention.dose: Twelve weekly individual sessions of approximately one hour.
intervention.provider: Trained local female nonspecialists, with expert and peer supervision.

comparator: Waitlist plus usual clinic/social resources; waitlist received IPT after the three-month comparison.

outcomes.name: Major depression diagnosis
outcomes.result: Lower odds with IPT plus usual care.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

outcomes.name: PTSD diagnosis
outcomes.result: Lower odds with IPT plus usual care.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

outcomes.name: Physical IPV among partnered participants
outcomes.result: Exploratory reduction; changing partnership and differential attrition limit interpretation.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

outcomes.name: Absenteeism
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

finding: At three months, IPT reduced odds of major depression and PTSD in the mixed-GBV cohort. Partnered-subgroup IPV findings were exploratory and vulnerable to attrition/relationship-status changes.
limitation: Sequence visible to coordinator; differential attrition and mixed GBV exposure. Later follow-up lacks an untreated comparison and cannot establish persistent comparative benefit.

design.randomizationEvidence: Excel-generated random color sequence in blocks of ten; coordinator assigned next color after baseline, with the next allocation visible.
design.crossRationale: One cross: explicit random allocation; double-blinded treatment not established.

quality.riskOfBias: Provisional assessment; allocation, masking and missingness limitations explicitly retained.
quality.attrition: At three months, 34/123 IPT versus16/133 control lost; overall90/256 did not complete all assessments. Completer primary data were also missing for13 IPT and1 control.
quality.confounding: Random assignment supports group comparison; implementation, missingness and analysis remain relevant.
quality.adverseFindings: Acute suicidality/GBV danger was screened and referred with escorted transport; systematic adverse-event totals not established.
quality.transferLimits: Sequence visible to coordinator; differential attrition and mixed GBV exposure. Later follow-up lacks an untreated comparison and cannot establish persistent comparative benefit.

title: Forgiveness Therapy to Build Hope and Reduce Anxiety and Depression in Battered Women in Pakistan.

relevance.population: Muslim women in a shelter screened for substantial domestic violence and psychological distress; partner and in-law abuse reported.
relevance.exposureEvidence: Muslim women in a shelter screened for substantial domestic violence and psychological distress; partner and in-law abuse reported.
relevance.rationale: Psychological intervention with explicitly reported domestic/IPV exposure; mixed-cohort transfer is qualified where applicable.
relevance.transferLimit: See population and limitations; not a population-wide recommendation.

setting: One shelter; residents from several Punjab cities.

sampleSize.description: See randomized and attrition fields; analyzed is model population when specified.

intervention.provider: Clinical-psychology master’s graduate with75 hours of forgiveness training; same researcher administered assessments.

comparator: No formal therapy; participants could seek informal help from the intervener.

outcomes.name: Depression, anxiety, anger, hope and forgiveness
outcomes.result: Benefit claimed; numerical gain-score inconsistencies prevent dependable effect extraction.
outcomes.uncertainty: Confidence intervals provided when source establishes them; otherwise unresolved.

finding: Authors report large symptom and hope benefits, but tables disagree about control-group changes, so quantitative efficacy cannot be accepted without clarification.
limitation: N=30, no active comparator or follow-up, researcher both therapist and assessor, and substantial baseline forgiveness imbalance. Gain-score tables conflict with reported pre/post means.

design.randomizationEvidence: Methods explicitly state random assignment,15 per group; sequence generation and concealment unspecified.

masking.assessors: Researcher/intervener administered self-report items, including orally for participants unable to read; independent masking absent.

design.crossRationale: One cross: explicit random allocation; double-blinded treatment not established.

quality.riskOfBias: Provisional assessment; allocation, masking and missingness limitations explicitly retained.
quality.attrition: Thirty participants appear in pre/post tables; no participant-flow accounting established.
quality.confounding: Random assignment supports group comparison; implementation, missingness and analysis remain relevant.
quality.adverseFindings: No systematic harms assessment established. The protocol distinguishes forgiveness from reconciliation but also encourages a gift/deed toward the offender; consequences are unreported.
quality.transferLimits: N=30, no active comparator or follow-up, researcher both therapist and assessor, and substantial baseline forgiveness imbalance. Gain-score tables conflict with reported pre/post means.
